context: Interactive hierarchical file system table with expand/collapse, search, sorting, and per-row sparkbar + donut encoding of size proportion relative to parent, across 6 color-coded top-level directories and ~200 items.
first_impression: Clean and readable at a glance — hierarchy is legible through indentation, colors are restrained, and the table structure imposes natural order.
what_works: The 6-color Tol palette maps one hue per top-level directory and carries through all children, making branch membership immediately traceable without a legend. Indentation depth (22px per level) cleanly separates root, top-dir, and sub-dir rows without ambiguity.
what_doesnt: Proportion (spark bar + %) and Share (donut + %) are redundant encodings of the same metric in adjacent columns, doubling visual complexity with no new information — one column should be dropped. The 20px donut charts are too small to read arc angle precisely and function only as decorative repetition of the percentage label beside them.
